question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expression by multiplying the equation through by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{8y+5}{3} & =6y \\ 3(\frac{8y+5}{3}) & =3\cdot 6y \\ \cancel{3}\cdot (\frac{8y+5}{\cancel{3}}) & =18y \\ 8y+5 & =18y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we solve the remaining equation using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}8y+5 & =18y \\ 8y+5-8y & =18y-8y \\ 5 & =10y \\ \frac{5}{10} & =\frac{10y}{10} \\ \frac{1}{2} & =y\end{aligned}
$$

Thus, $y=\frac{1}{2}.$
